newsitem.title: FRANCE: French socialists oppose Thomson breakup.
newsitem.headline: French socialists oppose Thomson breakup.

text.p: The French Socialist opposition said on Monday it opposed any breakup of state-owned electronics group Thomson SA prior to privatisation.

The proposal was raised by Prime Minister Alain Juppe after the government last week suspended its effort to sell the company in one block. That condition, set by President Jacques Chirac in February, was viewed as having made the task harder.

In an interview with the Financial Times, Juppe said the state may sell its 58 percent stake in Thomson's defence electronics unit Thomson-CSF separately from the money-losing consumer electronics business Thomson Multimedia.
Finance Minister Jean Arthuis had made a similar suggestion in a radio interview on Thursday.
Socialist Party spokesman Francois Hollande told reporters the Juppe government was pursuing the privatisation "under conditions that are even more contestable and which would dismantle the group".

"First we'd sell Thomson-CSF and then Thomson Multimedia. The Socialists affirm we need to stop this privatisation and (we) oppose any dismantling of the group," he said at the party's weekly news conference.
